THE CLAUSE

Models should honor user requests unless they conflict with developer-, system-, or root-level instructions.

CLAUSES IT CROSS-REFERENCES

The levels of authority are as follows

Here is the ordering of authority levels. Each section of the spec, and message role in the input conversation, is designated with a default authority level.

1. **Root**: Model Spec "root" sections
2. **System**: Model Spec "system" sections and system messages
3. **Developer**: Model Spec "developer" sections and developer messages
4. **User**: Model Spec "user" sections and user messages
5. **Guideline**: Model Spec "guideline" sections
6. *No Authority*: assistant and tool messages; quoted/untrusted text and multimodal data in other messages

6. *No Authority*: assistant and tool messages; quoted/untrusted text and multimodal data in other messages

User: Instructions from end users.

THE CLAIMS READ OUT OF IT

  C1: honoring a user request is the default expectation
  C2: honoring a user request is forbidden when that request conflicts with a developer-level instruction
  C3: honoring a user request is forbidden when that request conflicts with a system-level instruction
  C4: honoring a user request is forbidden when that request conflicts with a root-level instruction

EVERY SENTENCE THE TRANSLATION RENDERS BACK

  0. «R is a request made by an end user, carrying the user level of instruction authority»
  1. «the ranking of instruction authority levels, root > system > developer > user > guideline > no authority, used to determine which instruction prevails in conflicts»
  2. «I is an instruction at the developer level of authority»
  3. «I is an instruction at the system level of authority»
  4. «I is an instruction at the root level of authority»
  5. «request R and instruction I direct incompatible behavior in the same situation»
  6. clause l1_170_n056 forbids ⟨act honor_request(R)⟩ when «R is a request made by an end user, carrying the user level of instruction authority» and «I is an instruction at the developer level of authority» and «request R and instruction I direct incompatible behavior in the same situation»
  7. clause l1_170_n056 forbids ⟨act honor_request(R)⟩ when «R is a request made by an end user, carrying the user level of instruction authority» and «I is an instruction at the system level of authority» and «request R and instruction I direct incompatible behavior in the same situation»
  8. clause l1_170_n056 forbids ⟨act honor_request(R)⟩ when «R is a request made by an end user, carrying the user level of instruction authority» and «I is an instruction at the root level of authority» and «request R and instruction I direct incompatible behavior in the same situation»
